newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai B shares slightly up at noon.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai B shares slightly up at noon.

text.p: Shanghai B shares were slightly up at noon on Wednesday with the market taking a breather after several days of sharp gains, brokers said.
The B index put on 0.527 points or 0.54 percent to 98.497 points on volume of 17.783 million shares worth $12.788 million, compared with $16.524 million on Tuesday morning.

Profit-taking emerged at high levels, preventing the index from further rises, brokers said. But they said that if there are no solid measures from the government to cool down the market, the the strong uptrend trend will continue in the short term.
"Investors are becoming cautious after the continued sharp gains, resulting in shrinking follow-up buying," one broker said.
"Investors are concerned Beijing may take measures to cool down the over-speculative A share market, which will certainly have a negative impact on the B shares," another broker said.
"If there are no such measures, the market is likely to continue to be strong," he said.
Of 43 B shares, 42 traded, with 16 up, three flat and 23 down.
Portable phone maker Eastern Communications was the star, surging $0.136 or 9.71 percent to $1.536 on volume of 1.1 million shares.

Market barometer Shanghai Lujiazui Finance & Trade Zone Development was the most actively traded on institutional support buying, rising $0.014 or 0.85 percent to $1.646 on volume of 1.6 million shares.
Shanghai's A share index was firmer in active trading, but the market trend is unclear due to doubts about Beijing's attitude, brokers said.
The index rose 7.597 points or 0.49 percent to 1,556.969 points on volume of 538.9 million shares worth 8.0 billion yuan.
The SSE30 blue chip index put on 50.032 points or 1.15 percent to 4,413.149 points.
Nanjing Panda Electronics was the star after long-term consolidation, soaring 1.10 yuan or 10.04 percent to 12.05 yuan on volume of 988,800 shares.
